---
title: "Install iblatlas"
---

`iblatlas` is a Python package. It needs **Python 3.10 or newer**. We recommend
installing it with `pip` into a virtual environment.

## Create an environment and install

A virtual environment keeps the packages for one project separate from your other Python
projects. Create one with the tool you use:

::: {.panel-tabset group="installer"}

## venv

`venv` is Python's built-in tool for creating an environment:

```bash
cd path/to/your/project        # move to the directory you will work from
python -m venv .venv           # create the environment in a folder called .venv
source .venv/bin/activate      # activate it; on Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install iblatlas           # install iblatlas into it
```

Each time you open a new terminal, activate the environment again:

```bash
cd path/to/your/project
source .venv/bin/activate      # on Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
```

To leave the environment, run `deactivate`.

## uv

[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) creates the environment and installs into it:

```bash
cd path/to/your/project        # move to the directory you will work from
uv venv --python 3.12          # create the environment in a folder called .venv
source .venv/bin/activate      # activate it; on Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
uv pip install iblatlas        # install iblatlas into it
```

Each time you open a new terminal, activate the environment again:

```bash
cd path/to/your/project
source .venv/bin/activate      # on Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
```

To leave the environment, run `deactivate`.

## conda

[conda](https://docs.conda.io/) creates a named environment, and `pip` installs `iblatlas` into
it:

```bash
conda create -n iblatlas python=3.12    # create an environment called iblatlas
conda activate iblatlas                 # activate it
pip install iblatlas                    # install iblatlas into it
```

Each time you open a new terminal, activate the environment again:

```bash
conda activate iblatlas
```

To leave the environment, run `conda deactivate`.

:::

The environment is only active in the terminal where you activated it. If it is not active,
Python will not find `iblatlas`.

## Check the installation worked

With the environment active, run:

```bash
python -c "import iblatlas; print(iblatlas.__version__)"
```

This should print a version number. If `pip` says it cannot find a matching version, or the
import fails, check which Python the active environment uses:

```bash
python --version
```

It needs to be 3.10 or newer. If it is older, install a newer Python from
[python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/) and create the environment again.

## Atlas data downloads automatically

Installing `iblatlas` does not download the atlas. There is nothing extra to run: the first time
your code or the GUI loads an atlas, the data downloads and is saved to your Downloads folder,
and later runs reuse it. For where the files go and how large they are, see
[Data downloads and caching](../explanation/data-downloads-and-caching.qmd).

## Save the atlas data somewhere else

The atlas data is saved in the cache directory of ONE, the IBL data-access package that installs
with `iblatlas`. To save it somewhere else, set that directory once, before first use:

```python
from one.params import setup

setup(silent=True, cache_dir='/path/to/cache')
```

The new location starts empty, so the next load downloads the data again. To reuse data you
have already downloaded, move the `histology` folder from
`~/Downloads/ONE/openalyx.internationalbrainlab.org/` into the new cache directory, keeping the
folders inside it, so that the files are in `<new cache dir>/histology/ATLAS/Needles/Allen/`.

## The IBL Atlas GUI

The IBL Atlas GUI is a desktop application for browsing the atlas. It needs extra packages that
draw its windows (`PyQt5`, `qtpy` and `iblqt`), which you install into the same environment:

::: {.panel-tabset group="installer"}

## venv

```bash
pip install "iblatlas[gui]"
```

## uv

```bash
uv pip install "iblatlas[gui]"
```

## conda

```bash
pip install "iblatlas[gui]"
```

:::

To open it, activate the environment and run:

```bash
atlas
```

A window opens with a view of the brain from above. The first time, it downloads the atlas if
you have not used it before. The `atlas` command only exists in the environment where you
installed the extra, so activate that environment first. For what the windows show and how to
use them, see [Explore the atlas in the IBL Atlas GUI](explore-the-atlas-in-the-gui.qmd).
